summary.bottom_line: Rising bond yields are pulling everything down before the open. Don't add anywhere today. I expect chips to win back part of their early drop and the big tech names to keep sliding.
summary.where_we_are: Thursday 20:03 SGT / 08:03 ET. US pre-market, opening in about 85 minutes. Singapore has closed. US weekly jobless claims are out at 20:30 SGT, and Micron reports on 1 Oct at 4:05am SGT.
summary.macro_attribution: The 10-year Treasury yield has moved the most: it closed at 5.11%, is about 5.15% this morning, and is at a 19-year high. Oil (+1.1% to $93.7) and the VIX fear gauge (+6.5% to 16.2) are secondary, and the dollar is flat. Today's call depends on the 10-year yield. Oil is not driving it.
what_happened: Chip stocks are down about 2% pre-market and the Nasdaq futures are down 1% (tape). I found no chip-specific news, only yields (CNBC, Sep 24). Pre-market trading has no volume behind it, so the move is thin until the open.

Taiwan did not sell off: its index was flat and TSMC in Taipei fell only 0.6% today (tape). Correction (20:13 SGT, before the 20:30 release): Korea is shut for a holiday today. The Samsung +3.2% and SK Hynix +1.2% first quoted here were Wednesday's session, before the US yield selloff, so they say nothing about today.

Yesterday had the same setup: Nasdaq futures were down 1% on yields (CNBC, Sep 23), but the chip index closed flat from 8pm while big tech kept falling (tape). Chips have now closed at or above their 8pm level four sessions running.
Chips are still stretched. They are up 12.7% in five days and 10% above their 50-day average (tape), which is why I say don't add even though I lean up.

The US–China trade truce has been extended to Jan 10, Treasury Secretary Bessent said as Xi's visit began (CNBC, Sep 24). That is mildly positive for Asia but not a chip story. Chip export controls are off the agenda.

per_group.semis: slightly up from here — dip buyers take back part of the 2% gap, with memory makers (Micron, SanDisk) leading.
per_group.big_tech: slightly down — the big platform names kept falling after yesterday's gap while chips held. Google and Amazon are already below their 50-day averages, and Meta is the most stretched (+22% above its 50-day).
per_group.sg_banks: flat at Friday's close — the index already took the yield hit today (-0.7%), and the trade-truce news offsets a soft US handover.
per_group.market: flat from here — the chip bounce and the big tech slide roughly cancel out.

change_my_mind: Jobless claims well under consensus (~201k) at 20:30 SGT push yields higher and flip chips to down.
If the 10-year yield closes above about 5.18%, that is a fresh leg up, and chips (the most stretched group) fall hardest. That flips chips to down.
If Micron and SanDisk are still red at 23:00 SGT, the dip bid is not showing up, and that flips chips to down.
If the 10-year falls back below 5.11%, everything bounces and the big tech call is wrong.
summary.confidence: low, because bond yields are driving the tape, a data print lands inside the window, and the chip call bets against the morning gap on a four-day pattern.
summary.cant_know: Whether today is the day the yield climb finally breaks the chip rally. It hasn't in four sessions, and that is the whole bet.
summary.the_call: Mixed, and mild. The market ends roughly where it opens. Chips win back some of the morning's drop (+0.5 to 1% from pre-market), led by memory. Big tech drifts lower, with Meta, the most stretched, taking the worst of it.
